mode: Vite development server, production Wasm artifact
method: Imported supplied save through the title UI, loaded it without construction edits, retained initial player camera, and captured the development diagnostic UI. Each capture uses a rolling 240-sample window; intervals measure requestAnimationFrame callback pacing, not confirmed displayed frames or GPU time. Simulation continues between captures. No production before/after baseline was collected.
visualChecks: Production build loaded the supplied file and rendered the factory, terrain, water, animals, and belts.
One pole drag placed four separated poles with visible connecting wires.
Ground panel displayed Grade / level, 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 m depths, white current-height outlines, coloured result plates, and completed a test stroke.
Steel smelter displayed separate Recipe ingredients and Fuel / heat compartments and the carbon explanation.
Switching from steel to copper preserved 16 Iron plate and displayed the leftover-input explanation.
A bridge drag into deep water displayed the specific depth refusal. Successful shore-skipping and every pole tier remain covered by native tests; they were not exhaustively replayed in the browser.
limits: Development JavaScript, embedded browser, short rolling windows, and no before/after browser baseline. Do not treat these captures as a production FPS guarantee or evidence of the speedup caused by the patch.
frameP95Us covers CPU preparation and WebGL submission, not asynchronous GPU execution.
Browser frame pacing includes scheduling and all main-thread work; it does not isolate DOM, Wasm, compositor, GPU, or host-browser overhead.
High and Low both ran near 30 callbacks per second; the cause of that cadence remains unisolated.
Forest radial growth and offscreen animation restoration are covered by automated regressions; long-duration forest evolution was not judged from this short UI session.
